protein: ASPA, aspartoacylase (cytosolic; hydrolyses N-acetyl-L-aspartate; loss of function causes Canavan disease), assayed as an ASPA-GFP fusion
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P45381), expressed in HEK293T
readout: -(toxicity score from competitive growth), the source score being 0 for growth like wild type and 1 for growth like the toxic reference variant C152W; negated here so that higher is less toxic
assay_method: VAMP-seq in a HEK293T landing-pad line. A site-saturated, barcoded cDNA library of ASPA fused to GFP was integrated as a single copy by Bxb1-catalysed recombination at the landing-pad locus; the promoterless plasmid also expresses mCherry from an IRES downstream of ASPA as a per-cell expression control, and non-recombinant cells were removed with AP1903 (rimiducid) via the landing pad's iCasp9. Instead of sorting, the recombinant pool was propagated under doxycycline and sampled at days 0, 5, 7 and 9; each variant's barcode frequency over time gives its competitive fitness. The toxicity score is the slope alpha of a linear regression of variant frequency against time, normalised as (alpha_i - alpha_WT)/(alpha_C152W - alpha_WT), so that the wild type reads 0 and the toxic reference variant C152W reads 1 by construction. Values are the mean of slopes over replicates.
remark: Readout is the tox_score column of Source Data sheet "All Variant Data", negated so that higher is better, because a lower toxicity score is the better outcome. Sequence is UniProt P45381 (human ASPA, 313 aa) fetched whole; the label check passes with bad = 0 across all 313 positions and all 5947 designed missense labels. The file holds missense substitutions only: the 313 nonsense variants of the same screen cannot be written as {WT}{pos}{MUT} against a protein sequence, and the 313 synonymous variants carry no score in this table. The wild-type row is written as 0.0, which is what the normalisation in the Methods defines rather than a measured value, and is stated as such in the paper. Phase 7: C152W, the variant the normalisation anchors at 1, reads exactly -1.000000 in this file after the negation, and its abundance score is 0.057, consistent with the paper's observation that every toxic variant is also low-abundance. One count does not reconcile: the paper reports toxicity scores for "5847 of 5947 (98%) missense variants and 307 out of 312 (98%) nonsense variants", while this sheet carries 5840 missense and 308 nonsense scores. This file follows the deposited table. Relatedly, the replicate-level subsets the paper quotes (951 non-toxic and 1529 toxic variants at toxicity score <0.4 / >0.6 with abundance score <0.2) come out as 750 and 1495 from the merged means published here; those figures were computed per replicate, and the per-replicate scores are not in this workbook. Not included as separate work items: the VAMP-seq abundance screen of the same library, which is a separate measurement and is curated as its own dataset under Stability/FoldingStability; the 106-tile degron screen of Fig. 5, whose units are 24-residue tiles rather than variants of ASPA; the low-throughput abundance validations (the low_troughtput_abundance_score column, 27 variants); and the RNA-seq differential expression of the same workbook, which is not a per-variant measurement. The gemme_de, normalized_rosetta_ddg, wcn_sidechains_AF, degrons, QCDPred and AF_confidence columns are predictions, not measurements, and the Clinvar and gnomAD columns are annotations.

protein: PG-1, protegrin-1 (18-residue cationic beta-hairpin antimicrobial peptide with two disulfide bonds)
source_organism: Sus scrofa (UniProt P32194, residues 131-148, the mature protegrin-1 peptide)
readout: -percent haemolysis of human red blood cells at 128 ug/ml; higher (less negative) means less lysis of mammalian membranes
assay_method: Haemolysis of single-donor human red blood cells. Peptide at 128 ug/ml was incubated with 1e9 cells/ml in PBS for 3 h at 37 C in biological triplicate; after centrifugation the supernatant absorbance at 540 nm was background-subtracted against PBS alone and divided by the absorbance of 1% Triton X-100 (defined as 100% haemolysis). Values are the mean of triplicates.
remark: Sequence is the mature protegrin-1 peptide RGGRLCYCRRRFCVCVGR, taken verbatim from the source tables, which list each variant as a full 18-residue sequence rather than a mutation code; it matches UniProt P32194 residues 131-148 exactly, and mutant codes here were derived by diffing each variant against it. The orientation is inverted for readout and normalized-score, because less haemolysis is the better outcome. Source is Supplementary Data sheet "Peptides for ML", column %Hemolysis, used as it stands. Phase 7: 27 of these peptides also appear in Source Data sheet "Fig 3C" with haemolysis re-reported to fewer digits; the two agree to within 0.031 percentage points, and regressing that sheet's log10 aggregation against its haemolysis reproduces the R2 = 0.63 the Fig. 3c caption states, to two decimals. Not included: the circular dichroism spectra of Fig. 2a-d and the haemolysis dose curves of Fig. 3b, which are spectra and curves rather than one number per variant; the 95,472 and 51,877 machine-learning predictions in Supplementary Data (predicted, not measured); and the kill curves, propidium-iodide uptake and mouse infection data of Figs. 4 and 6, which cover four variants at most.
